body:
`scripts/preflight-release-tag.sh` is the documented "Gate before tagging" and it now refuses a
commit lacking bookkeeping OR a green CI verdict. But nothing mechanically invokes it.

    grep -rn "preflight-release-tag" scripts/ LOOP.md ~/.claude/skills/
      LOOP.md:176   **Gate before tagging: `bash scripts/preflight-release-tag.sh ...` must pass.**

That is the only reference in the entire workspace — one line of prose. No script calls it, no
skill calls it, and there is no pre-tag hook, because releases are cut by a model running
`gh release create` directly rather than by a release script.

So the gate's enforcement depends entirely on the tick reading LOOP.md §6 and choosing to run
it. A tick that is compacted, in a hurry, or working from a summary can cut a tag without ever
invoking the guard, and nothing will notice — the tag is immutable and the release is never
retracted (CLAUDE.md), so there is no downstream check to catch it either.

This is the shape where a gate exists, is documented, is tested, and still does not fire: the
tests prove the script refuses correctly, not that anything asks it to.

Options, none of them free:

  - A `release-guard.yml` workflow on `push: tags: v*` that re-runs the same assertions and,
    on failure, immediately deletes the tag before the release build publishes. Racy, and
    deleting a tag is itself the retraction the policy forbids.
  - A workflow on tag push that does not delete but pages loudly and marks the release draft.
    Cheap, catches it after the fact rather than before.
  - Wrap tag creation in `scripts/cut-release.sh` that runs the preflight and then
    `gh release create`, and make LOOP.md name only that script. Mechanical, but only binds
    ticks that use it — same prose dependency one level up.

Recorded rather than chosen because the tradeoff is about how the release train is driven,
which is the operator's call. Related: the gate itself landed 2026-08-12 (outer workspace
commit 94190a0) and is verified end-to-end against live GitHub — replaying it against v4.1.31's
commit refuses on both the bookkeeping and the CI axis.
title: The release-tag gate is invoked only by prose, so a tick can simply not run it
